Marathon Petroleum stock fell 5.5% today to $373.86, extending a sharp two-week decline that has wiped out nearly 5% of its value. The timing tracks closely with escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran has launched direct military strikes against U.S. targets in the Gulf region, disrupting confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a stable energy corridor. While crude oil prices remain relatively firm (U.S. benchmark at $89.53/barrel), the threat to shipping and refining operations in one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints appears to have spooked investors, outweighing the fact that U.S. refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity.

The sell-off also comes as refinery margins face headwinds from softer demand signals. Record diesel prices are now driving inflation higher in developed economies, which typically precedes reduced consumption as central banks tighten policy—a dynamic that could pressure refining profitability in coming months even if crude prices stay steady.
